source_text: Educet sicut lumen iustitiam tuam et iudicium tuum sicut meridiem. Sicut sensus lucem appetunt, ita iustus lumen iustitiae ostendetur sole iustitiae — caelo et terrae.
thought_title: The just one shown as light by the sun of righteousness
orientation: Origen is commenting on Psalm 37:6, explaining how the just person's righteousness and judgment will be brought out like light and midday.
pass_a_gloss: May he lead out as light your justice and your judgment as midday. As the senses light they seek, so [the] just [man] [the] light of justice will be shown by [the] sun of justice — to heaven and [to] earth.

choices.why: Future indicative, matching the psalm's promise that God will bring out righteousness; keeps the active force of God as agent.
The psalm's simile is retained exactly; 'like light' preserves the comparison without turning it into identity.
Appetunt has the force of desire or longing, not mere seeking; 'long for' captures the natural inclination Origen describes.
Ablative of agent or means; 'by the sun' shows the sun of righteousness is the instrument through which the just one is shown.
Dative of reference or advantage; the showing is directed toward heaven and earth, so 'to' preserves the dative force.

bible_refs.note: Educet sicut lumen iustitiam tuam et iudicium tuum sicut meridiem

pass_b_english: He will bring out your righteousness like light, and your judgment like midday (Psalm 37:6). Just as the senses long for light, so the just one will show forth the light of righteousness by the sun of righteousness—to heaven and to earth.

problems.quote: so the just one will be shown by the sun of righteousness—to heaven and to earth.
problems.source_quote: ita iustus lumen iustitiae ostendetur sole iustitiae — caelo et terrae.
problems.why: Ostendetur means 'will show/display,' not passive 'be shown by'; sole is dative/instrumental 'by the sun,' but sense is active shining.
problems.fix: so the just one will show forth the light of righteousness by the sun of righteousness—to heaven and to earth.
problems.ruling: 'lumen iustitiae' omitted; 'ostendetur sole iustitiae' means 'shown as/by sun of righteousness,' not just 'shown by the sun.'

edits.old: so the just one will be shown by the sun of righteousness—to heaven and to earth.
edits.new: so the just one will show forth the light of righteousness by the sun of righteousness—to heaven and to earth.

fixed: Corrected mistranslation: 'ostendetur' is middle/passive in form but here means 'will show/display,' and 'lumen iustitiae' is the object shown, not the just one being shown by the sun. The English now reads 'so the just one will show forth the light of righteousness by the sun of righteousness—to heaven and to earth.'

last_rejected.quote: He will bring out your righteousness like light, and your judgment like midday (Psalm 37:6).
last_rejected.source_quote: Educet sicut lumen iustitiam tuam et iudicium tuum sicut meridiem.
last_rejected.why: Source is second person ('your righteousness'), English shifts to third person ('He will bring out your righteousness'), changing who speaks.
last_rejected.fix: Bring out your righteousness like light, and your judgment like midday (Psalm 37:6).
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'Educet...iustitiam tuam' is Psalm 37:6 (Vulgate 2nd person); 'He will bring out your righteousness' is standard, not a speaker shift.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'sole' is ablative of 'sol' (sun), but context demands 'by/through the sun of righteousness' as agent; however 'sole' could be dative. The English 'by' makes sun the instrument, but Latin likely means 'before the sun of righteousness' or 'to the sun of righteousness'.
last_rejected.fix: before the sun of righteousness—to heaven and to earth.
last_rejected.ruling: 'sole iustitiae' is ablative; 'by the sun of righteousness' is a reasonable rendering of ablative means/agent. No clear error.
